meta.title: Apple
meta.subtitle: How strong is the business behind the stock?
meta.coverage_universe: Apple Inc.; consolidated US GAAP financials
meta.decision_use: Historical business and industry analysis; not a stock-price valuation

executive_view.headline: A stronger mix, a smaller share base — but modest top-line growth.
executive_view.summary: Apple’s historical strength is the combination of product scale, higher-margin Services and substantial cash generation. The numbers support business durability more clearly than rapid organic growth. They do not establish whether the stock is attractively priced.

panels.title: Services did most of the incremental work
panels.text: Revenue growth was modest, but the mix improved. Services supplied most of the net revenue increase and earned a substantially higher gross margin than the company overall.

panels.title: EPS grew faster than the business
panels.text: Higher net income and fewer diluted shares both contributed. The bridge separates the two mathematically; the share-count effect is not a measure of buyback effectiveness, because employee equity issuance also affects the denominator.

panels.title: Cash generation is strong, not steadily rising
panels.text: Free cash flow remained substantial, but did not compound at the pace of EPS. Five-year cash distributions roughly matched cumulative free cash flow. The balance sheet provides context for the small excess of distributions over that measure.

watches.title: Services growth and gross margin
watches.text: Monitor whether Services continues to outgrow total revenue without deterioration in its gross margin. A slowdown would weaken the principal historical source of mix improvement.

watches.title: iPhone demand and Greater China
watches.text: Track iPhone revenue alongside Greater China revenue. Neither geography nor product revenue discloses unit volume, so changes cannot automatically be attributed to device demand or market-share losses.

watches.title: Cash returns versus cash generation
watches.text: Compare cash buybacks plus dividends with free cash flow, net liquid assets and diluted shares. Repurchase authorizations are not cash expenditure, and fewer shares do not by themselves establish attractive repurchase prices.

methods.title: Periods and units
methods.text: Fiscal years end in September, not December. FY2023 contains 53 weeks; the other years shown contain 52. Dollar charts use billions; underlying facts use millions. All figures are historical nominal US dollars.

methods.title: What free cash flow means here
methods.text: Operating cash flow less cash payments for property, plant and equipment. This is an analyst-defined non-GAAP measure, not cash available after every obligation. Cash-flow-statement buybacks include settlement timing and can differ from the repurchase note.

methods.title: EPS bridge and tax distortion
methods.text: The sequential bridge applies net-income growth first at the FY2021 share count, then the share-count change at FY2025 net income. Order matters; the reported-EPS residual is shown rather than hidden. FY2024 included a one-time net tax charge, so FY2025 EPS growth is not a clean run-rate comparison.

methods.title: Scope of the conclusion
methods.text: No current stock price, valuation multiple, total shareholder return or forecast is used. Net cash excludes leases and other obligations; marketable securities are not all immediately available cash. Business quality is not the same as an attractive entry price.
